summary: 1933 International Derrick fire tower, about 80 feet, moved from Orangeburg, South Carolina to Ferncliff Forest in Dutchess County, New York, in 2007; open to visitors.

facts.design: 1933 International Derrick fire tower made of Carnegie steel

access.note: Open every day of the year; an easy walk of about 15 minutes from the Ferncliff Forest parking lot.

visit.trail_note: Easy walk of about 15 minutes from the Ferncliff Forest parking lot; about 120 feet of elevation change

events.note: Astor family built a stone overlook in or around 1912; its foundation remains on the site
1933 International Derrick fire tower; the Register's build year
Army built a 40-foot wooden tower during the war, per the Register
Register says the 1942 wartime tower was taken out of service in 2000
Blog and Wikipedia put the removal of the wartime tower (deemed unsafe) in 2006; the Register says 2000
Moved from Orangeburg, South Carolina to Ferncliff Forest; the Register says moved in 2007, the blog says constructed in summer 2007 and gives no move date
Registered January 16, 2016 as US 1117, NY 37; nominated by Homer Staley
Chapter newsletter (May 2023) describes an April 2023 visit: criminals had been at work across the tower (cab, roof, footings, steel); the writer had arranged a graffiti paint-over

notes_for_editor: Solid on the 1933 derrick tower, its origin in Orangeburg, South Carolina, the 2007 move and the NHLR visit-report details (NHLR, blog and the FFLA list agree). Disagreements left open in the story: removal of the 1942 wartime tower is 2000 in the Register but 2006 in the blog and Wikipedia; the Register says moved in 2007 while the blog says constructed that summer; the Register calls the wartime tower a 40-foot wooden tower and Wikipedia calls it an enclosed tower. Record's events 2019 and 2021 ('restored', graffiti painted out) were not verified: no source in the cache or read for those years, so they are not in the research events. The 2023 newsletter describes vandalism and a planned paint-over; it does not clearly confirm the paint-over was completed, so the event is worded as the visit finding. Record's 2007 'relocated' event was missing its year; 2007 is set from the Register. Climbability is inferred from the NHLR's description of an open overlook with stairs OK in the 2018 visit report; no current staffing source (the Register's staffing answer reads 'No Response'). A search summary named a contractor and a 79-foot replacement tower; this was not verified on any page read and is not used. No photos added: the Register's photo is credited to Homer Staley with no licence stated.
